ranking_rule: Never rank across layers. Compare only within: item vs item, material vs material, item+material vs item+material.

methodology.seasonality_test: Kruskal-Wallis on year-normalised monthly values, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted over items x 2 sources.
methodology.phase_offset: peak_month_id - peak_month_kr (mod 12); reported only if adjusted ID p < 0.05 and amplitude >= 0.20.
methodology.lebaran_test: Wilcoxon signed-rank, paired per Eid cycle (-6..+3 months); BH-adjusted over 12 items. Interpretation uses the adjusted p-value.
methodology.forecast_method: Rolling-origin CV, horizon 3, expanding window. Gate baseline pre-registered = persistence. Candidates: Holt-Winters, XGBoost (clipped 0-100). Validated only if mean MASE gain > 0, block-bootstrap 95% CI > 0, and gain >= 10% of baseline MASE.
methodology.lag_analysis: EXPLORATORY ONLY, not used in this JSON; no item survived FDR.
methodology.multi_horizon: EXPLORATORY extension of the single-horizon gate to 1/3/6/12 months. 48 tests, BH-corrected. Not part of the pre-registered gate.

pitch_summary.headline: 1 of 12 items pass the pre-registered 3-month forecast gate; 6 items have a reliable KR-to-ID phase offset. Extended to 48 tests across 4 horizons, 0 survive BH.

data_quality.keyword_type_mix: Some Google Trends files mix Topic entities (capitalised, e.g. 'Cotton', 'Polyester') with search terms (lowercase, e.g. 'katun'). Topics can dominate the 0-100 normalisation and compress search-term variation. Re-downloads on a separate day showed the trends were similar, so the mix is treated as an acceptable approximation for this MVP and documented as a limitation rather than fixed.

best_single_result.note: Strongest single signal across 48 tests; does not survive Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

multi_horizon.headline: Extended from 12 pre-registered tests (horizon 3 only) to 48 tests across horizons [1, 3, 6, 12]. 2 test(s) pass the raw gate; 0 survive BH correction. We report 0 of 48 validated.
multi_horizon.methodology_note: Origins every 3 months (expanding window); 12-step forecasts sliced to h. Block bootstrap block = ceil(h/3) origins (min 3). One-sided bootstrap p, then BH across all 48 tests. Exploratory only — not part of the pre-registered single-horizon gate.

limitations: Naver and Google keywords are not semantically equivalent.
Phase offset may reflect shared year-end seasonality, not adoption lag.
Forecast values exist only for validated items (1 of 12); the rest are reported as not validated, by design.
Forecast confidence intervals are block-bootstrap based and approximate; fold autocorrelation is not fully corrected.
Google anomaly month(s) ['2026-02'] were masked (causal forward-fill): Google spiked across unrelated items while Naver was flat. Reconfirmed by re-downloading three affected items.

Some Google Trends files mix Topic entities (capitalised) with search terms (lowercase) in one comparison. Topics can dominate the 0-100 normalisation and compress search-term variation. Visual re-downloads showed similar trends; treated as an MVP approximation.
China is not tracked (Baidu Index requires a Chinese phone number).
denim_jacket has no parent material because denim fabric is not tracked.
Sep-2026 covers 28/30 days for the six oldest Naver files; treated as complete.
Lag analysis is exploratory; p-values are not robust to method choice.
Multi-horizon backtest is exploratory; not part of the pre-registered single-horizon gate. 0 of 48 tests survive BH correction.
Findings specific to 2017-2026; not generalizable without validation.
